segments.label: EXPLAINER: the spine and the three tools (Ava, opening)
segments.vo_script: Every Sunday, Ken Long answers three questions before he looks at a single trade. What kind of market is this? How much of my capital does the evidence permit? And which way is the index leaning right now? This course gives you his three laconic tools for those three questions. The spine is a three by three matrix: market direction, bull, sideways or bear, against volatility, quiet, normal or volatile. The cell you are in decides what the week permits. On that spine hang the tools. The ETF2 theoretical exposure model, which turns a table of ten regions into one percentage. The SPY daily parabolic SAR flip, which says wait or initiate. And the kata patterns, which name the turn when it comes. Four hours, in the order he uses them. Then the week that is on the screen right now.

segments.label: Explainer: the grid, drawn
segments.vo_script: The label Ken reads first on page one is Van Tharp's market type, as Ken applies it. Two questions, nine answers. Direction: where did the S and P close against its two-hundred-day moving average? More than two percent above: bull. Within two percent: sideways. More than two percent below: bear. Volatility: where does today's fourteen-day A T R percentage sit among the last one hundred days? Inside one standard deviation of the average: normal. The top sixth: volatile. The bottom sixth: quiet. Three by three. In Ken's thirty-year test, the next day was up on average in four cells: every bull cell, and sideways quiet. Down in the three bear cells. Flat in sideways normal and sideways volatile. The words at the top of the report, bullish normal, name one of these nine cells. Everything else in this course is read after that label.
